message.reasoning:
We need to write JUnit 4 test cases for JsonSchemaFactory covering all methods. Must not mock, use real objects. We need to test builder, building factory, getInstance, checkVersion, normalizeMetaSchemaUri, isYaml, idMatchesSourceUri, getSchema methods (string, InputStream, URI with cache). Use simple schemas JSON strings.

We need to create a JsonMetaSchema instance. There are static builders: JsonMetaSchema.builder(String uri). Probably need to provide a meta-schema. Use JsonMetaSchema.getV4() for simplicity. That returns a built-in meta-schema. Ensure defaultMetaSchemaURI matches its URI. Use JsonMetaSchema.getV4().getUri().

Test building factory with builder: set objectMapper, yamlMapper, defaultMetaSchemaURI, addMetaSchema, build. Verify fields via reflection? Not needed; we can call getUriFactory, getUriTranslator, getSchema.

Test checkVersion returns appropriate classes; test unsupported throws IllegalArgumentException.

Test normalizeMetaSchemaUri converts to https scheme and strips fragment/query: provide http URL with userInfo and port.

Test isYaml: create URI with .yaml, .yml, .json, no extension.

Test idMatchesSourceUri: need a JsonMetaSchema and schema node with $id matching given URI. Use simple JSON: {"$id":"http://example.com/schema"} . Use meta schema's readId method to get id. Use factory.idMatchesSourceUri via reflection (private). Could use reflection to invoke. That's allowed.

Test getSchema(String) parses JSON and returns JsonSchema. Validate that schema is created (not null). Use simple schema {"type":"string"} and then validate a JSON value.

Test getSchema(URI) with caching: need a schema accessible via classpath URL fetcher. Use a resource file in test resources. Provide a simple JSON schema file packaged in classpath. Use URI "classpath:/test-schema.json". Use builder default meta schema V4, addMetaSchema, ensure classpath URL factory/fetcher present by default. Then call getSchema(uri) twice and ensure same instance returned when cache enabled. Use == comparison.

Also test cache disabled: builder.enableUriSchemaCache(false) and ensure different instance.

Test exception handling: getSchema with invalid JSON string should throw JsonSchemaException.

We need to reference JsonSchemaException class; assume available.

Write tests with @Test and expected exception.

All code must be in one file enclosed between ###Test START## and ###Test END##.

Let's craft.

Will need imports: org.junit.*, com.networknt.schema.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.dataformat.yaml.YAMLMapper, java.io.*, java.net.URI, java.util.*.

Implement helper method to read resource InputStream.

For reflection: use java.lang.reflect.Method to invoke private idMatchesSourceUri and isYaml? isYaml is private, we can use reflection.

But we can test isYaml indirectly via getSchema with a .yaml file. Simpler: reflection.

Write test class JsonSchemaFactoryTest.

Proceed.
